artifacts.summary: Confirms the routing_agents_hard->hard_contracts migration premise (all six -hard agents reduce to standard-agent + injected contracts), catalogs the full blast radius beyond the dispatch's named scope, and surfaces two independent pre-existing defects (a deploy-time contracts-directory clobber and a dangling extension-namespaced @-import path) that share root cause with this task's own hard_contracts wiring work.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system, a manifest's provides.context entry for a bare top-level directory name (e.g. "contracts") merges additively across extensions at deploy time by directory-level copy, not per-file dedup -- two extensions declaring the same directory name with overlapping basenames silently clobber each other, with the winner determined by extension load order. Verify any shared-directory provides.context entry for basename collisions before relying on it for per-domain overrides; use the hard_contracts replace:/additive mechanism (flat, domain-prefixed basenames under the shared directory) instead of a separate same-named directory per extension.

check-extension-docs.sh Rule G (dangling .claude/context/contracts/*.md reference scan) only matches the literal substring ".claude/context/contracts/" immediately after ".claude/" -- it does not catch an extension-namespaced variant like ".claude/extensions/<ext>/context/contracts/*.md", which never exists in the deployed tree (per-extension deploy dirs under .claude/extensions/<name>/ contain manifest.json only, never a context/ subtree). Any future dangling-contract-reference check should account for this path shape explicitly.
